summary: Brick light on Hockamock Head at the entrance to Burnt Coat Harbor, Swan's Island, Maine. First lit 1872 as a range pair; automated 1975; restored by the town and a friends group.

structures.note: Square, tapered brick tower, 32 ft to the middle of the lantern (nomination).
Smaller square brick front range tower; LighthouseFriends says it was tipped into the sea on 1 August 1883. The nomination says the front light was discontinued in 1884 and later removed.
One-and-a-half-story, L-shaped clapboard keeper's house (nomination; archive gives L-shape Cape Cod, 1872).
Small tapered bell house holding the striking machinery for the fog bell; the bell was cast by Meneely, West Troy, N.Y. (LighthouseFriends).
Fourteen by twenty feet, with boat-hoisting gear (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Grounds open; keeper's house and tower open in summer, Tuesday to Saturday 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. (LighthouseFriends). Reached by the Swan's Island ferry from Bass Harbor.

stay.note: Upstairs apartment in the keeper's house, available for weekly rental in summer since 2017 (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Town of Swan's Island (owner); Friends of the Swan's Island Lighthouse (non-profit restoration group)

events.note: Range pair of square brick towers and the keeper's house built (nomination).
First lit 15 August 1872 (LighthouseFriends).
Fourth-order Fresnel in the rear tower; fifth-order in the front tower (LighthouseFriends). Archive gives fourth order, 1872.
Station dory capsized on an outing; a visiting Boston woman, Mrs. Cutler, drowned (LighthouseFriends only).
Covered walkway, 80 feet long, built between the two towers.
Front range tower jacked up and tipped into the sea on 1 August 1883 (LighthouseFriends). The nomination gives 1884 for discontinuing the front light.
Front range light discontinued (nomination).
A vessel was wrecked 'last year' while trying to make the harbor by the range lights, per the Board's fiscal 1893 report (scan p.53). Vessel not named. The year 1892 is inferred from 'last year'.
Brick oil house built (nomination; archive).
Bell house and automatic striking machinery installed.
Station electrified; siren whistle foghorn installed after electrification.
Automated by the Coast Guard.
Fourth-order Fresnel removed; automatic light placed on a nearby skeleton tower.
Automatic 250 mm optic returned to the lighthouse, 18 December 1978.
Tower stripped of peeling paint and sealed to save money (instead of regular repainting); repainted white after complaints.
Transferred to the Town of Swan's Island after Congress approved the legislation. LighthouseFriends gives 1994 in another passage.
Shingle siding of the bell tower replaced by the town.
Restoration of the keeper's house begun, supported by grants and private gifts (LighthouseFriends).
Solar-powered LED optic installed (VLB-44).
Tower restoration (2016-2019, $85,000 National Maritime Heritage grant) and oil house restoration (2020 grant) completed (LighthouseFriends).

wrecks.outcome: Wrecked while trying to make Burnt Coat Harbor by the range lights, per the Board's fiscal 1893 report ('last year'). The year is inferred from that phrase.

corrections.why: The nomination gives 32 feet from the base to the middle of the lantern, which is 9.8 m. The record's 10.0 m appears to be a rounding of the overall height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The archive prints Roscoe M. Chandler's stint as 1560-1943. The first date is a typo. LighthouseFriends dates his keeping from 1932 to the early years of the Second World War, and this story and the JSON use 1932.

notes_for_editor: (1) Front range tower: LighthouseFriends says it was tipped into the sea on 1 August 1883; the nomination says the front light was discontinued in 1884 and later removed. Unresolved. (2) Transfer to the town: LighthouseFriends gives 1993 in one passage and 1994 in another; the story gives both. (3) The archive's Roscoe M. Chandler line (1560-1943) is a typo; the story and JSON use 1932 from LighthouseFriends. The archive record itself should be reported to the USLHS, not corrected here. (4) The 1871 Light-House Board quotation (harbor 36 miles from safe anchorage) is taken from the nomination, which quotes it. The 1871 report is not in the local corpus; the story footnotes the nomination for it. (5) LighthouseFriends describes Allen's logbook, held by the National Archives. We have not read the logbook; the story attributes its contents to LighthouseFriends. (6) Single-source items: the 1876 drowning of Mrs. Cutler and the 1902 Prohibition rescue are from LighthouseFriends only. A Chronicling America search for 'Burnt Coat Harbor' with 'Prohibition' and 'Milan' failed with HTTP 520 errors from loc.gov; the search for 'Burnt Coat Harbor' alone returned 86 Maine pages, which were not checked against these events. (7) The record's characteristic (Oc W 4s) and range (9 nm) are not in any source read; they are omitted from the facts. (8) The Green Island light proposed in the 1893 report is not followed up; its outcome is not established by any source read. (9) The record says the tower is 10.0 m; the nomination's 32 ft gives 9.8 m (see corrections). (10) Post-1960 keepers appear only as the archive prints them in the roster. Frank Milan, the keeper's son who wrote a 1974 book (per LighthouseFriends), is named only as a child born at the station. (11) The Lighthouse Board's fiscal 1896 and 1900 entries also record the dwelling and roadway work (scan pages 50 and 47); the 1900 sewer-pipe entry matches LighthouseFriends' date for the sewer pipe. The story does not use the 1900 entry. (13) Fiscal-year fix (fact-check 2026-10-22): the ice, communication and roadway entry (no. 22) is on scan p.346 of annualreportlig01statgoog. That volume's fiscal 1893 report starts at scan p.8 and its fiscal 1894 report at scan p.302, so p.346 is in the report for the year ended June 30, 1894. The draft had labelled it fiscal 1893; source 4 now says 1894. The fiscal 1893 entry (scan p.53) holds the 'one range light discontinued', 'vessel wrecked last year' and Green Island text. (14) The $500 legal and road request is in the reports for fiscal 1894, 1895 and 1896 (and later); the story cites 1894 and 1896. (15) The 'newspaper interview' with Nettie Milan is LighthouseFriends' account of an unnamed newspaper; the story footnotes LighthouseFriends and does not name a paper. (16) Restoration dates (2006 start, 2016-2019 tower, 2020 oil-house grant, 2021 completion) and the 1982 paint decision are LighthouseFriends' statements; the nomination and archive do not give them.
